newsitem.title: FINLAND: New world record in Finnish wife-carrying race.
newsitem.headline: New world record in Finnish wife-carrying race.

text.p: A burly oil worker bore his tiny wife around a 236-metre obstacle course on Saturday to set a new world record in this Finnish village's unique wife-carrying contest.

Jouni Jussila, 29, and his wife Tiina took home 45 litres of beer -- the equivalent of her weight -- along with other prizes after he pounded over the punishing course carrying her piggyback in one minute, five seconds to retain the World Championship title for a second year.
"If the woman starts laughing, it's all over," Tiina told journalists before the race.
The bizarre annual summer contest pits some 30 couples in a challenge to heft a female around the village school playground. She need not be a wife but must be over 17 and wear a crash helmet.

A crowd of about 5,500 cheered, howled and mustered the occasional Mexican wave as the men ran with their partners -- by piggyback, fireman's lift, or even with both legs astride the shoulders. Only one man collapsed under the strain.
The course, through a chest-high pool of water and over two wooden stiles, also drew competitors from Germany, Switzerland and Estonia.
The sport was started in 1991 in this village in central Finland and thrown open to global challengers last year.
Many newcomers paid the penalty of inexperience, plunging headlong into the water or losing grip on their partners and forfeiting a 15-second penalty.
Villagers and competitors dismissed any suggestion of political incorrectness in the idea of the contest, which organisers say stems from local legend.
"This is our tradition," said a woman named Liisa.
Wife-Carrying started when the local tourist authority rediscovered the 19th-century tale of Ronkainen the robber, said to have held a test for would-be gang members.
He apparently forced them to lug sacks of grain or live swine over a similar course. Some in Sonkajarvi also refer to a much older tribal practice -- stealing other men's wives.
"There should be some craziness in life," said spectator Taru Harjunpaa, a 32-year-old secretary from Helsinki.
The winning couple also won a mobile phone, a loaf of local bread and a wooden statue modelling their winning piggyback style.
